\[

w_p(fg)=w_p(f)+w_p(g).
\]

\[
w_p(f)+w_p(g)\ge 0.
\]

\[
v_p(f_i g_j)\ge w_p(f)+w_p(g)\ge 0.
\]
Thus $f_i g_j$ has nonnegative $p$-adic valuation for every prime $p$. Since $f_i g_j\in\mathbb{Q}$, it follows that $f_i g_j\in\mathbb{Z}$.
\end{proof}

\end{proof}

\[
\min_k v_p((fg)_k)=\alpha_p+\beta_p.
\]
Because $fg\in\mathbb Z[x]$, every coefficient $(fg)_k$ has nonnegative $p$-adic valuation. Hence
\[
\alpha_p+\beta_p\ge0.
\]

For arbitrary $i$ and $j$, we have $v_p(f_i)\ge\alpha_p$ and $v_p(g_j)\ge\beta_p$, so
\[
v_p(f_i g_j)=v_p(f_i)+v_p(g_j)\ge\alpha_p+\beta_p\ge0.
\]
This holds for every prime $p$. Therefore $f_i g_j$ is a rational number with nonnegative valuation at every prime, which implies $f_i g_j\in\mathbb Z$. Since $i$ and $j$ were arbitrary, the desired conclusion follows.
\end{proof}
